dea-med-001.text: Events JSON They're coming in. Kinesis Data Firehose and are delivered to S3 for consultation with Athena. The queries are expensive and slow because the files are JSON The team wants the data already CHEGUEM to S3 in column format, without adding components. Which configuration resolves?
options: Enable the format conversion of Firehose itself to Apache Parquet, using a Glue Catalogue Date
Create a cluster EMR to convert files after delivery
dea-med-001.explanation: A) Incorrect: DMS is bank migration, no streaming delivery. B) Correct: Firehose converts JSON→Parquet/ORC In the case of the product concerned, the data are used in the same way as for the product concerned. Athena. C) Incorrect: larger buffer changes file size, not format. D) Incorrect: works, but adds cluster and cost, violating requirement.

dea-med-002.text: A stream of the Kinesis Data Streams in Provisioned Mode suffers ProvidedThroughputExceededException at peak times, and the traffic pattern is unpredictable. What change eliminates manual capacity management?
options: Change partition key to constant value
Migrate stream to mode ON-DEMAND, automatically dimensioning capacity
dea-med-002.explanation: A) Incorrect: duplicate streams divides the architecture and does not solve the root. B) Incorrect: constant key creates A hot shard and worsens everything. C) Correct: on-demand shards scale mode automatically according to traffic — ideal for unpredictable loads. D) Incorrect: retention affects storage/replay, not write limit.

dea-med-003.text: A daily job of the AWS Glue reprocessed TODOS the historical files of a prefix of the S3 to each execution, increasing cost and duration. Which feature makes the job process only new data since the last execution?
dea-med-003.explanation: A) Incorrect: versioning protects objects, does not control the scope of the job. B) Correct: bookmarks track what has already been processed (archives/partitions), making the executions incremental. C) Incorrect: Schedule Registry versiona streaming schemes. D) Incorrect: more DPUs accelerate unnecessary reprocessing — the cost continues.

dea-med-004.text: Business analysts SEM Spark knowledge need to clean and standardize spreadsheets (remove duplicates, standardize dates, treat null) with a visual interface, before making them available in the data lake.?
options: AWS Glue DataBrew, with visual transformations ready
Write PySpark jobs in Glue Study
dea-med-004.explanation: A) Incorrect: Lambda with pandas is pure code and has time/memory limits. B) Incorrect: notebooks EMR require code and cluster. C) Correct: DataBrew offers 250+ visual transformations (profile, cleaning, normalization) without writing code, generating reusable recipes. D) Incorrect: requires Spark code — audience is analyst without code.

dea-med-005.text: An Oracle on-premises bank migration to the AWS It needs downtime of a few minutes. The bank receives continuous writing. AWS DMS enable it?
options: Full load unique at the weekend
Full load + CDC (change data capture), replicating the changes continuously until the time of the cutter
Export dump SQL and import manually
Snapshot of the restored storage in AWS
dea-med-005.explanation: A) Incorrect: a single full load loses the writings that occur during and after loading. B) Correct: the DMS load everything and then apply the changes in almost real time (CDC) — the cutover only turns the point of the application. C) Incorrect: dump/import generates hours of unavailability. D) Incorrect: storage snapshot is not portable between machines/managed environments..

dea-med-006.text: A Spark job runs 2 hours per night. Today the cluster EMR It's on. 24/7 "to ensure." Which architecture change drastically reduces the cost by keeping the job running?
options: Schedule the job for business hours
Adopt clusters TRANSIENTES: create the cluster for the job (data no S3 way EMRFS) and close it automatically at the end
Fold the size of the knots to the job finish faster
dea-med-006.explanation: A) Incorrect: HDFS higher increases cost and links the data to the cluster. B) Incorrect: the time does not change the 24c) Correct: with data on S3 (EMRFS), the cluster becomes disposable — only the ~2D) Incorrect: we increase the cost per hour.

dea-med-007.text: A team needs to calculate aggregations in windows of 1 minute (e.g. total sales per minute) on a stream of Kinesis EM TEMPO REAL, sending the results to dashboards. Which service performs this continuous processing with status and windows?
options: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
dea-med-007.explanation: A) Correct: o Managed Flink (ex-Kinesis Data Analytics) processes streams with time windows, status and SQL/Java/Python — the case of exact use.: Athena consult data at rest in S3, no streams on the move. C) Incorrect: Crawler catalog metadata. D) Incorrect: QuickSight view; does not process streams.

dea-med-008.text: Producers publish Avro events in a topic and the schemes evolve frequently, breaking consumers. VALIDAR and VERSIONAR the schemas centrally, controlling the compatibility of the changes.?
dea-med-008.explanation: A) Incorrect: versioning of the S3 is of objects, not schema contract. B) Correct: the Registry schema records and versions schemas (Avro/JSON/Protobuf) of streams, applying compatibility rules (backward/forward) in evolution. C) Incorrect: Data Quality validates the DADOS, not the evolution of the streaming scheme. D) Incorrect: Config audit resource configuration AWS.

dea-med-009.text: A pipeline records individual events on S3, generating thousands of files of few KB per day. Athena were slow even with Parquet and partitions. What is the cause and correction?
options: The S3 limits the amount of files per bucket
Failure to activate the Acceleration Transfer
The problem of SMALL FILES: excessive tiny files generates overhead per object; correction is compact/group into larger files (ex.: 128 MB+) via Firehose buffer or compaction jobs
dea-med-009.explanation: A) Incorrect: Parquet is the preferred format of Athena. B) Incorrect: there is no practical limit of objects per bucket. C) Incorrect: Transfer Acceleration is upload, not analytic reading. D) Correct: each file has fixed list/opening cost; millions of small files kill performance. Larger buffers in intake and periodic compaction jobs solve.

dea-med-010.text: The same stream of the Kinesis needs to feed a real-time analysis consumer and allow new consumers to reread the events of the last 7 days (reprocessing). Which configuration attends?
options: Kinesis Data Streams with extended retention for 7 days, allowing multiple consumers and replay
Kinesis Firehose data with backup enabled
dea-med-010.explanation: A) Correct: Data Streams retains records (24standard h, extendable to 365 (b) Incorrect: Firehose delivers and does not allow rereading of the stream. SQS no replay. D) Wrong: SNS it's immediate push, no rereading retention.

dea-med-011.text: A company needs to move 400 TB of historical data for the S3 in 3 weeks, with internet link of 200 Mbps. Which solution meets the deadline?
dea-med-011.explanation: A) Incorrect: parallelism does not create extra band. B) Incorrect: DataSync optimizes, but 400 TB a ~200 Mbps would take months. ~1 week asks the Snow family; devices are sent, loaded locally and returned. D) Incorrect: acceleration via edge does not change the contracted physical band.

dea-med-012.text: A team wants to execute ETL Spark sometimes a day, SEM manage clusters and without optimizing infrastructure, accepting the cost by DPU. Another load requires custom native libraries, runtime control and specific instances with Spot. What services do they provide, respectively?
options: EMR for the first; Athena for the second
Lambda for the first; Glue for the second
AWS Glue for the first case; Amazon EMR for the second
dea-med-012.explanation: A) Incorrect: Athena does not rotate ETL Arbitrary Spark with native libraries. B) Incorrect: Lambda has 15 min limit and not Spark. C) Correct: Glue = Spark serverless with minimal effort; EMR = Total control (AMIs, native libraries, fleet Spot). D) Incorrect: or Glue does not control runtime/instances/Spot required in the second case.
